title: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO
summary: Coal India's Mahanadi Coalfields IPO (also known as the MCL IPO) is a ₹8,981.12 crore book-built issue priced at ₹129–₹136 per share, to be listed on BSE and NSE. It is open from November 19 to November 23, 2026, with allotment expected on November 25 and listing on November 27, 2026. The minimum investment is ₹14,960 for 110 shares.

Mahanadi Coalfields IPO reservation details show category-wise allocation of shares. Out of the total 66,18,36,300 shares, approximately 17% are reserved for QIB, 12.75% for NII, 29.75% for retail investors, 5% for employees, 10% for shareholders, and 25.5% for anchor investors.
Mahanadi Coalfields IPO reserves up to ₹900.1 crore of the issue for shareholders of Coal India (10% of the issue).

To apply in the shareholder category, you must have held at least one Coal India share in your demat account as on November 13, 2026, the record date for the shareholder quota (the date of the Mahanadi Coalfields Red Herring Prospectus). The shares must be in a demat account linked to the PAN you apply with. Only Coal India shares count; shares of other Coal India subsidiaries such as Bharat Coking Coal (BCCL) do not qualify. Only individuals and HUFs can apply in this category.
In the shareholder category you can bid up to ₹2 lakh. You can bid at the cut-off price. There is no discount on the issue price in this category.

Eligible Coal India shareholders can apply in the shareholder category and also in the retail or HNI category with the same PAN. Holding Coal India shares makes you eligible to bid in the shareholder category; it does not guarantee an allotment.

The record date has passed. Shares bought on the exchange are credited to your demat account one trading day later (T+1), so Coal India shares bought on or after November 13, 2026 do not make you eligible.

Incorporated in April 1992, Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd. is India's largest coal producer by volume, which engages in the mining and production of non-coking coal. It operates mostly in the Talcher and Ib Valley coal fields located in Odisha State, and produces different grades of coal that include washed and beneficiated coal for use in the power sector and industries like cement, sponge iron, steel, aluminum, and paper. · · Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd. is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Coal India Limited. The formation of Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd. is aimed at increasing the production of coal to meet the growing demands for energy in India. It operates a combination of open-pit and underground mines along with coal handling plant, rapid loading system, silos, and coal evacuation infrastructure. As on June 30, 2026, the Company has 17 mines that include 14 opencast mines and three underground mines. · · As on June 30, 2026, Mahanadi Coalfields has a total of 20,473 permanent employees that include executives, workmen, staff and supervisors in different departments like mining, engineering, excavation, finance, human resources, environment, marketing, and others.
Government of India, Coal India Ltd. are the company's promoters of Mahanadi Coalfields.

Mahanadi Coalfields Limited has allocated 16,87,68,255 equity shares to anchor investors at ₹136 per share, raising ₹2,295.25 crore ahead of its IPO. · · The allocation was made to 53 institutional investors, led by Life Insurance Corporation of India (24.75% of the anchor portion), Nippon India Mutual Fund, Tata AIG General Insurance, Invesco India Mutual Fund, WhiteOak Capital and HDFC Mutual Fund. Domestic mutual funds received 8,95,22,070 shares (53.04%) across 29 schemes, and life insurance companies and pension funds received 4,45,03,615 shares (26.37%).

sections.h: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO - Strengths and Risks

b.p: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO strengths and risks highlight key business factors, financial position, and market sentiment that may impact investor interest.

Single Largest Coal Producing Company in India: The Company is India’s largest single coal producing company, contributing 21.00% of the coal produced in India in Fiscal 2026, and having sufficient audited coal reserves for approximately 45 years at current production levels.

Technical and Financial Support from Coal India Limited: As a subsidiary of Coal India Limited, which is the world’s largest coal producer, the Company has the benefit of technical know-how, manpower, technology and improved market standing, which facilitate large-scale projects.

Low Cost Mechanised Mining: The Company has its mines in Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields, which allow for predominantly open cast and mechanized mining operations with high surface miner operations, along with coal evacuation through rail, road and port facilities.

Revenue Dependence on Non-Coking Coal Sales: The main source of revenue is non-coking coal, which constituted 97.38%, 97.13%, 97.41%, 97.10% and 99.94% of sale of products in the periods under review; reduction in demand would significantly impact the company.

Revenue Dependence on Thermal Power Sector: Sales to the thermal power sector, consisting of state, central GENCO and IPP customers, were between 68.62% and 70.60% of sale of products in the periods under review, thereby making the Company vulnerable to demand changes in that sector.

Revenue from Government-Owned Customers: Revenue from government-owned and controlled power generation companies and utilities accounted for up to 47.64% of revenue from operations in the periods under review, making the Company vulnerable to regulatory scrutiny and collection problems, including large dues pending from Andhra Pradesh power companies.
